item.title: This Undiscovered Wisconsin City Is Becoming a Surprisingly Sophisticated Weekend Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just 90 miles from Chicago, Beloit, Wisconsin, is emerging as an unexpected destination for travelers seeking a weekend getaway with boutique accommodations, ambitious dining, historic architecture and a growing entertainment scene. The launch of Beloit Bound, a new travel-inspiration platform, puts the city’s transformation into focus through curated itineraries, insider recommendations and original destination storytelling. Along the Rock River, this small Wisconsin city offers a collection of distinctive stays, including the MICHELIN Key-recognized Hotel Goodwin, the industrial-chic Ironworks Hotel and the wine barrel suites at Hidden Creek Estates. Its culinary scene features restaurants from the acclaimed Geronimo Hospitality Group, rooftop dining and traditional Wisconsin supper clubs, while entertainment ranges from professional baseball at ABC Supply Stadium to duckpin bowling, golf and gaming. Design enthusiasts can also explore the historic College Park neighborhood and Grand Avenue, where restored homes and architectural character tell another part of Beloit’s story. With major investment reshaping the city, including the development of Ho-Chunk Gaming Beloit, the destination offers a fresh perspective on Midwest travel and an appealing alternative to more familiar weekend escapes.

The Curated Take

Some of the most interesting destinations are the ones travelers haven’t quite put on their radar yet. Beloit’s appeal is its unexpected combination of historic preservation, contemporary hospitality, independent businesses and a developing culinary and entertainment scene. Rather than relying on a single attraction, the city is building an experience around discovery, with boutique hotels, distinctive architecture and places to linger over a memorable meal. For travelers who enjoy finding the next interesting place before everyone else does, Beloit makes a compelling case for a Midwest weekend getaway.

item.title: New York Celebrates Women Shaping the Culinary World
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For five decades, Les Dames d’Escoffier New York has championed the women shaping the worlds of food, wine and hospitality through education, mentorship and philanthropy. The founding and largest chapter of Les Dames d’Escoffier International marks its 50th anniversary in 2026 with a gala on November 9 at The Lighthouse at Pier Sixty in New York City, honoring celebrated chef, restaurateur and television personality Lidia Bastianich. The evening brings together an impressive collection of culinary talent, including Daniel Boulud, Eric Ripert, Marcus Samuelsson and Jacques Torres, alongside a series of mentor-and-mentee pairings that spotlight the importance of supporting the next generation of women in the industry. Since its founding in 1976, the organization has awarded more than 1,000 scholarships and distributed over $2 million in educational support, while building a professional community spanning chefs, restaurateurs, sommeliers, farmers, writers, educators and hospitality leaders. The anniversary celebrates not only its history, but also the women whose expertise and leadership continue to influence the culinary landscape.

The Curated Take

Food travel is often framed around celebrated chefs, acclaimed restaurants and memorable dining experiences, but the people shaping those experiences deserve recognition, too. Les Dames d’Escoffier New York offers a glimpse into the broader community of women whose work influences culinary culture, hospitality, wine, education and the future of food. Its 50-year milestone is particularly meaningful because it celebrates both achievement and the importance of opening doors for those who follow. In a field where mentorship and the exchange of knowledge help preserve traditions while encouraging innovation, that legacy reaches well beyond the kitchen.

item.title: Four International Awards Put Vietnam’s Ha Long Bay Luxury Cruises on the World Stage
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Grand Pioneers Halong Bay Cruise has earned four international titles in 2026, reinforcing Vietnam’s growing presence in the luxury cruise market and bringing renewed attention to the extraordinary seascape of Ha Long Bay. The Vietnamese cruise brand received World’s Best Green Cruise Line and Asia’s Best Cruise Line at the World Cruise Awards, alongside Best Bespoke Yacht Cruise in Asia and Best Cruise Liner in Asia at the World Luxury Travel Awards. The recognition marks the third consecutive year Grand Pioneers has been honored by the World Cruise Awards, following its wins in 2024 and 2025. Launched in late 2023, the cruise combines spacious accommodations with private balconies, dining, wellness facilities, a Sea Spa and a four-season saltwater pool. Its environmental initiatives include seawater-cooled air conditioning, low-emission engines and advanced wastewater treatment systems, reflecting an effort to balance luxury hospitality with greater environmental responsibility. Developed by Viet Thuan Group, the fleet also represents a distinctly Vietnamese approach to cruise tourism, with the country’s maritime heritage and natural landscapes at the center of the experience.

The Curated Take

Ha Long Bay’s dramatic limestone formations and emerald waters have long made it one of Southeast Asia’s most recognizable natural landscapes. Experiencing the bay aboard an overnight luxury cruise offers a different perspective, allowing travelers to remain immersed in the scenery as the light changes and the day unfolds. Grand Pioneers’ four international awards are notable not only for the recognition of its onboard experience, but also for the attention they bring to Vietnam’s evolving luxury hospitality sector. Its emphasis on environmental technology is particularly relevant in a destination where preserving the natural setting is essential to the future of tourism.

item.title: Bali Invites Travelers to Rediscover the Island Through the Healing Power of Water
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From the Indian Ocean shoreline of Jimbaran Bay to the lush Ayung River valley, Four Seasons Resorts Bali is inviting travelers to experience a quieter, more contemplative side of the island through The Season of Sacred Water, a collection of wellness, cultural and culinary experiences running from October 2026 through March 2027. Rooted in the spiritual significance of water in Balinese life, the program explores the island’s relationship with nature through traditional herbal drink-making, sound rituals and restorative spa treatments. At Jimbaran Bay, Tides of Renewal draws inspiration from the coast, with jamu-making and a treatment accompanied by the sounds of the ocean and Balinese gongs. At Sayan, Flow into Stillness turns toward the river and forest, pairing conversations about wellbeing with meditative rest in a suspended silk hammock and treatments incorporating local herbs and traditional instruments. Together, the two settings offer a more immersive approach to Bali wellness travel, one shaped by the island’s living traditions and natural landscapes.

The Curated Take

Bali’s appeal has never rested solely in its beaches or beautiful resorts. Its spiritual traditions, relationship with the natural world and distinctive approach to daily rituals offer a deeper dimension of discovery. What makes this collection compelling is the way it interprets those traditions through two very different landscapes. Jimbaran Bay offers the restorative presence of the sea, while Sayan brings guests closer to the rhythms of the river valley. For travelers seeking meaningful wellness experiences, this is an invitation to encounter Bali at a gentler pace, with time to listen, learn and reconnect.

item.title: The Way We Travel Is Changing: 8 Luxury Travel Trends Shaping 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Luxury travel in 2027 is becoming less about how many places travelers can see and more about how deeply they experience them. According to Audley Travel, its premium clients are increasingly seeking journeys shaped by emotion, personal interests and meaningful human connection. The company’s latest travel trends reveal a growing appetite for experiences that deliver an adrenaline rush, alongside quieter escapes and opportunities to discover destinations beyond their familiar highlights. Travelers are looking toward lesser-visited regions such as Japan’s Iya Valley, French Polynesia’s Austral Islands and China’s Tiger Leaping Gorge, while families are embracing itineraries that balance shared experiences with time for individual interests. Slow travel continues to gain ground, from extended stays in a single country to walking safaris and coastal cruises, while off-season journeys offer a different perspective on popular destinations. Evening experiences, from firefly encounters in Bali to illuminated Cambodian temples, are also attracting interest, as are return visits that combine land exploration with river and expedition cruising. Together, these shifts suggest a new direction for luxury travel in 2027: more personal, more flexible and increasingly defined by the feeling a journey leaves behind.

The Curated Take

Perhaps the most interesting shift in these predictions is the growing importance of intention. Travelers are looking beyond the familiar checklist of landmarks and asking what they want a journey to bring into their lives, whether that means a sense of adventure, time together as a family, cultural understanding or simply the freedom to slow down. The renewed interest in lesser-visited places and alternative seasons also points to a more considered approach to discovery. For luxury travelers, the next great journey may not be about going farther or doing more, but about choosing experiences that feel genuinely their own.

item.title: Five Years of Gracious Luxury: Raffles Bali Celebrates Its Place on Jimbaran Bay
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Since opening in December 2021, Raffles Bali has cultivated a distinctive expression of luxury on the hillsides above Jimbaran Bay, where 32 private pool villas are set across 23 hectares of tropical gardens overlooking the Indian Ocean. Celebrating its fifth anniversary in December 2026, the resort reflects on five years shaped by attentive butler service, cultural discovery, wellness and a deep connection to its surroundings. Guests can explore the island through botanical walks and wellness experiences, while its dining collection brings together Indonesian culinary heritage at Rumari, the immersive Rumari Counter and the coastal flavors of Peru at Loloan Coastal Peruvian. Recognized with Two MICHELIN Keys in both 2025 and 2026, Raffles Bali marks the milestone by looking ahead to its next chapter of hospitality on one of Bali’s most evocative coastlines.

The Curated Take

The appeal of Raffles Bali lies in an approach to luxury that gives equal weight to privacy, place and personal connection. Its setting above Jimbaran Bay provides a sense of retreat, while its culinary and cultural experiences offer ways to engage with Bali beyond the villa. Five years in, the resort’s continued recognition suggests that gracious hospitality is not simply about beautiful surroundings, but about the thoughtful details and human encounters that make a stay memorable.

item.title: A Design-Forward Hideaway in Portsmouth Just Earned New England’s Boutique Hotel Honors
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the heart of downtown Portsmouth, New Hampshire, Hotel Thaxter is earning recognition for its distinctive approach to boutique hospitality, having been named New Hampshire’s Best Boutique Hotel in Boston Magazine’s 2026 New England Travel Awards. Set within a historic building just steps from Market Square, the 15-room property pairs original architectural details with contemporary interiors, bold colors and thoughtfully selected furnishings. Its residential-style suites, some with full kitchens and separate living areas, make it appealing for both weekend escapes and longer stays along New Hampshire’s Seacoast. Guests are also within easy walking distance of Portsmouth’s independent shops, galleries, theaters, restaurants and waterfront, while the hotel’s own Nichinan restaurant adds a contemporary Japanese dining experience just downstairs. The award brings fresh attention to a destination where historic character, an independent dining scene and a walkable downtown make for an appealing New England getaway.

The Curated Take

Portsmouth has the kind of character that rewards a stay rather than a quick stop. Its historic streets, independent businesses, waterfront setting and lively culinary scene give visitors plenty of reasons to linger. Hotel Thaxter’s appeal is its connection to that atmosphere, offering a design-conscious place to return to after a day exploring the city. For travelers planning a New England escape, it is a reminder that a memorable stay does not always require a grand resort. Sometimes the right boutique hotel puts the best of a destination just outside the door.

item.title: Canadian Travelers Are Still Hesitant About U.S. Trips, Despite a Slight Rebound in Interest
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Canadian travel to the United States remains below its earlier levels, according to the latest October 2026 tracking study from Longwoods International. The survey found that 31% of Canadian travelers had visited the U.S. in the previous six months, little changed from a year earlier, while 18% had canceled planned trips. More notably, the share reporting no U.S. travel during that period rose to 51%, compared with 47% a year ago. There are signs of a potential recovery, however, with 47% of respondents saying they intend to visit the United States within the next 12 months, up from 39% in April 2025. Among those not currently planning a trip, 70% said an improved political relationship between Canada and the U.S. would make them more likely to visit, while 40% pointed to a more favorable exchange rate. The findings highlight the influence of cross-border relations, travel costs and currency fluctuations on Canadian tourism demand, a significant consideration for U.S. destinations and hospitality businesses that depend on visitors from their northern neighbor.

The Curated Take

The Canadian market remains an important part of the U.S. tourism landscape, and these findings suggest that rebuilding traveler confidence will require more than destination marketing alone. Political sentiment, affordability and the value of the Canadian dollar are shaping decisions about where and when to travel. The increase in stated intentions for the year ahead offers some encouragement, but the growing share of travelers who have recently stayed away is a reminder that destinations cannot take this neighboring audience for granted. For U.S. hotels, tourism boards and travel businesses, the opportunity lies in understanding what is keeping Canadian visitors at home and addressing the factors that could bring them back.

item.title: Beyond the Menu: Seabourn Is Making Destination-Inspired Dining Part of the Journey
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For luxury travelers, discovering a destination often begins at the table, and Seabourn is expanding that connection with the introduction of Earth & Ocean, a culinary philosophy that brings regional flavors, exceptional ingredients and food-focused exploration into the cruise experience. Building on the Earth & Ocean restaurant concept introduced in 2018, the philosophy will influence menus and programming across the fleet, pairing locally inspired dishes with carefully selected gourmet ingredients from around the world. In The Restaurant, a new Chef’s Market Finds approach will highlight regional ingredients and specialties reflecting each ship’s itinerary, from wild seafood in Alaska to fresh snapper in Australia and New Zealand. The program will also extend beyond onboard dining through chef-led experiences, local market visits, regional seafood celebrations, scenic cruising brunches and other culinary encounters designed to introduce guests to the food traditions and distinctive flavors of the destinations they visit.

The Curated Take

Food can offer one of the most immediate and memorable ways to understand a place. A regional ingredient, a traditional preparation or the influence of a particular coastline can reveal something about a destination that extends well beyond its landmarks. Seabourn’s Earth & Ocean philosophy recognizes that connection, making culinary discovery an integral part of the voyage rather than simply an onboard amenity. For travelers who value both exceptional dining and a deeper sense of place, the approach adds another dimension to luxury cruising, bringing the character of each destination to the table.

item.title: Discover Australia Through the Stories of Its First Peoples
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Australia’s most meaningful cultural journeys often begin with the people who know its landscapes best. The latest edition of Connect to Country, the digital publication from Discover Aboriginal Experiences, invites travelers to explore the country through the knowledge, traditions and perspectives of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander guides. Issue 12 journeys from the ancient rock art landscapes and rainforests of the Worimi people to sunrise experiences at Uluru, a Djiringanj ceremony on Yuin Country in New South Wales, and an early morning cruise through Kakadu’s Yellow Water Billabong. Other stories explore the enduring relationship between coastal communities and oysters, the history of the pearl trade on Western Australia’s Dampier Peninsula, and the ways Traditional Custodians have sustained their cultures through generations of change. The edition also connects luxury travelers with First Nations-led experiences paired with stays from Luxury Lodges of Australia, demonstrating how cultural understanding can become an essential part of a sophisticated Australian travel experience.

The Curated Take

Cultural travel becomes richer when the experience moves beyond observing a place to understanding the people, histories and traditions that have shaped it. First Nations-led tourism offers an opportunity to encounter Australia through perspectives that cannot be found in a conventional destination guide, from ancient knowledge of the natural environment to stories carried through dance, food, language and ceremony. For luxury travelers, these experiences bring depth and context to journeys through Australia’s extraordinary landscapes, while placing the voices of Traditional Custodians at the center of the story.
